archetypes.name: ledger-contract
archetypes.rationale: The plan hinges on a new timing-ledger row kind and strict attachment semantics that can silently drop or misattach data if schema details drift.
archetypes.prompt_body: Inspect the proposed ledger row contract, timing-report aggregation, and test/docs updates for mismatches against the existing timing ledger/report implementation. Focus on whether the 13-column `round` schema, skill/step/interval matching, nested child-step bounds, and JSON-only `rounds` emission are all planned consistently across scripts, docs, and harnesses. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: handoff-lifecycle
archetypes.rationale: Deferred timing emission across main-agent handoff paths is a cross-script lifecycle risk not fully covered by generic review personalities.
archetypes.prompt_body: Review the plan for gaps in the main-agent-vote and coder-main-agent handoff lifecycle across implement and design flows. Verify that starts are persisted once, preliminary rows are avoided, final counts come from post-adjudication artifacts, and durations include prompt-side apply/check/lint/commit work before re-entry. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: publish-freshness
archetypes.rationale: The run-log flush and design publish path has freshness and ordering requirements that can fail even if per-round telemetry works locally.
archetypes.prompt_body: Examine whether the plan correctly carries per-round data from temporary ledgers into committed run-log timing-report batches for both implement and design. Pay special attention to design publish ordering, stale `timing-report-final.json` removal or atomic replacement, existing flush sites, and whether the proposed changes avoid adding unnecessary publication paths. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.
